articles.title: Marsh Landing Asks Council for Speed Limit Change
articles.deck: The vote came after 23 residents spoke at Wednesday’s session.
body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Public works estimates the work will take about 23 weeks once it starts in January.

Councilmember Roman Hallinan asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $18,500. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

Residents of Marsh Landing said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.

articles.title: Vincent Reyes, 88, Longtime Crossing Guard
articles.deck: Friends remember Vincent Reyes for the many years of service to Kettle Hill.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Stonebridge Trail Crew in his or her name. Vincent Reyes died in July at home on Hazel Place, at the age of 88.

Born in Kettle Hill in the years after the war, Vincent Reyes spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Kettle Hill.

articles.title: Letter: The Bus Shelter on Juniper Lane Needs Attention
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. To the editor: I have lived on Juniper Lane for 39 years, and I want to say what a difference the Eastgate Senior Lunch Program has made.
Please keep the bus shelter in the budget. Many of us on Juniper Lane use it every week. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the May meeting.
